title: 1. Diagnose whether curl removal replaces sustained roll with reversals
hypothesis: Removing capture curl weakens directional contact, causing repeated axial-spin reversals rather than merely slower unidirectional rotation.

prediction.against: R-068 frozen R-046 parent on the same archived fresh cases
prediction.rationale: Count hysteretic axial-direction reversals per in-play second over each pair's common pre-drop interval; an increase of 0.5 reversals per second would identify a substantial directional instability behind the clamp's slow-spin failures.

code_changes: New lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/axial_reversals.py (numpy only) and scripts/isaac/axial_reversals.py: read the archived R-068 traces (parent_fresh.npz, zero_curl_fresh.npz, parent_promotion.npz, zero_curl_promotion.npz: per-step spin_rate, length, completed) and their rows; exit without collecting anything if a record is missing. No simulator, no LLM.

Frozen definitions: signed axial rate = env spin_rate (rad/s). A direction is held when |spin| exceeds the hysteresis band (1.0 rad/s) with the same sign on 3 consecutive steps; a reversal is a change of held direction. Rate = reversals per in-play second (60 Hz) over each pair's common pre-drop window (min of the two lengths). Primary: paired zero-curl minus parent reversal rate over the 160 fresh pairs with the 95% t interval (metric phase_transitions); secondary: the same over the 30 promotion pairs; also per-arm reversal rate, held-direction fraction, mean |spin| on the common window, and the archived sustained success and drops.

Prediction: increase of at least 0.5 reversals per second; refuted if the paired interval's upper bound is below +0.5; an interval spanning the threshold is inconclusive and one spanning zero is not evidence of increased reversals. Reversal counts alone cannot establish lost traction as the cause (limitation).

falsified_by: The paired interval's upper bound is below +0.5 reversals per second; an interval spanning the threshold is inconclusive, and one spanning zero is not evidence of increased reversals.

notes: Primary, predeclared (160 fresh pairs): zero-curl minus parent reversal rate +0.1622 [+0.051, +0.273] reversals per in-play second (48 wins, 50 losses, 62 ties). An increase is established, but the upper bound is below the +0.5 threshold: the prediction is refuted. Absolute rates 0.394 vs 0.232 per second, i.e. about 2.1 vs 1.2 reversals over a 5.2-second common window.
Promotion pairs (30): -0.0291 [-0.270, +0.212], no difference (0.346 vs 0.375 per second).

Both arms hold a direction on about 95% of in-play steps on both panels; the clamp's mean |spin| on the common window is 3.92 vs 5.25 rad/s on fresh (5.13 vs 6.40 on promotion). The zero-curl controller's slow-spin failures are therefore mostly slower unidirectional rotation, with a small, established increase in direction reversals, not a directional instability.
Reversal counts cannot establish lost traction as the cause (predeclared limitation); the audit says what the failure looks like, not why.
Accounting: 0 episodes, 0 LLM calls, about 1 min of CPU on the box. No deviation from the approved protocol.

An increase is established but small: about one extra reversal per 5-second window. Both arms hold a direction on 95% of in-play steps, and the clamp's mean |spin| on the common window is 3.92 vs 5.25 rad/s, so its slow-spin failures are slower unidirectional rotation rather than directional instability. Confidence 0.9: exact paired computation on archived data, 160 pairs, definitions frozen.
